history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED: no source found for any temple or shrine of Thangjing at Andro village. Every documented seat of Thangjing (Thangching) worship is elsewhere: the primary Thangjing Temple at Moirang, Bishnupur district (seq 2446b) on the banks of Loktak Lake, and the sacred hilltop shrine at Thangjing Hill in Churachandpur district, plus the main temple atop that peak. Andro's own religious landscape is centred on Panam Ningthou (seq 2444b) and the village's twelve other deities, and none of the sources consulted name a Thangjing shrine among them. The most likely reading is that this CSV row is a mislabeling - possibly a duplicate/confusion with the famous Ibudhou Thangjing Temple of Moirang (2446b), or with another Andro shrine. Recorded here as a thin placeholder at Andro village level pending review: consider merge with 2446b or removal. FLAGS: (1) unverified identity - no web footprint; probable CSV mislabeling; (2) CSV 'state' column held the town name (Andro) - real state is Manipur; (3) coordinates are Andro-village level only; (4) deity, festivals, hours, construction date all undocumented - verify.

name: Temple of Thangjing, Andro
town_description: Andro is an ancient village and nagar panchayat in Imphal East district, Manipur, about 25 km east of Imphal in the foothills of the Nongmaiching range. It is earmarked as a Scheduled Caste village and is renowned as a heritage destination: the home of the Loi people (among Manipur's earliest settlers), famous for its unique Charai Taba coil pottery made by married women, the Mutua Museum cultural complex, the Santhei Natural Park, and the ancient Panam Ningthou shrine with its ever-burning sacred fire.
